claims.statement: The schema is split between a baseline (db/init/02_schema.sql, run automatically on first boot of the bundled Postgres or once via make db-init-remote) and forward-only migrations in db/migrations/ that carry every later change; the baseline is deliberately not rewritten as a migration 0000, and schema changes go only in new migration files.

backend/app/db/migrate.py applies pending *.sql files in sorted filename order, each in its own transaction together with its schema_migrations ledger insert (version, 16-char SHA-256 checksum); a failure rolls back that file and stops the run, while a checksum mismatch on an already-applied file is reported as DRIFT but is not fatal; --status only lists.

Migrations are not automatic: make migrate/migrate-status run the runner explicitly, make up auto-migrates only for ENV=local with the bundled postgres service (and make seed depends on migrate only locally), and against managed databases migrating is a separate deliberate step.

Two migration files are numbered 0044 (0044_news.sql and 0044_one_read_policy_and_fk_indexes.sql); both are kept because the runner keys on the full file name and staging had already applied 0044_news, so neither should be renamed.

At boot the lifespan runs _verify_sql_catalog: verify_against_db raises RuntimeError and aborts startup when the SQL catalog lists a table or column missing from the live database, or a catalogued column that authenticated cannot SELECT (or a table anon reads only in part); extra live tables or columns do not fail boot, and live tables in neither CATALOG nor KNOWN_EXCLUDED are only logged at INFO and stay invisible to the SQL tool.

KNOWN_EXCLUDED in the SQL catalog deliberately withholds sensitive or bookkeeping tables (LangGraph checkpoints, users, threads, org_members, proposals, Import run/review bookkeeping, vault_research, funder_matches, deleted_documents, schema_migrations, graph_ingest_log), and tests assert the most sensitive are not readable and that withheld columns such as contacts.email are absent even from the star expansion.

Fact tables carry a common provenance block (source_url, source_name, fetched_at, content_hash, extractor_version from the baseline, plus as_of, document_id and archive_url added by 0001_provenance); source_url is always set while document_id links to documents only when content is stored, and as_of is distinct from fetched_at.

The SQL catalog derives which tables expose provenance from the presence of source_url/source_name/fetched_at columns, and Import's expectations.py (backend/app/ingest/research) derives researchable fields from the same catalog while treating provenance columns as tool-filled rather than researched.

promotions and catalog_writes (0041) form the undo log for Import saves: a trigger app.log_catalog_write() records old and new row JSON for a fixed list of catalog tables only while sangam.promotion_id is set, and later tables such as document_links (0047) attach the same trigger.

Three private Supabase Storage buckets exist: source-archive and org-vault (50 MB, created by 0020) and staff-sources (100 MB, created by 0032 with a staff-only read policy); the bucket migrations are guarded to no-op when there is no storage schema, as in the local container.

Supabase Storage is one project, so a local backend is kept out of the deployed buckets only by STORAGE_BUCKET_SUFFIX (for example -local), which is appended to every bucket name on the wire while documents.storage_path keeps the plain name; Settings.bucket_suffix ignores it when DATABASE_URL is the Storage project's own database, and boot warns when Storage is enabled with no suffix and a database outside the Storage project.

documents.storage_path is stored as bucket/key; archived source documents get a fetch-time key from the URL hash and content SHA-256 and are renamed at promotion to a per-entity year-based key, so objects left under hash folders were fetched but never cited, while vault keys lead with org_id and are not content-addressed because uploads go browser-to-Storage via signed URLs.

The storage integration is optional and non-fatal: with SUPABASE_URL or SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY unset calls are no-ops, helpers return None/False/empty on HTTP failure rather than raising (read being the exception that raises on Storage errors), and split() rejects unknown buckets and dot or empty path segments.

Neo4j via Graphiti is optional and derived: the graph is enabled only when NEO4J_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY are set, graphiti_core is imported lazily, and make graph-seed rebuilds it from Postgres rows (funder and org profiles, funder_activity partner lines, score_adjustments) as deterministically named episodes, so nothing may live only in the graph.

app.db.replicate copies data between two databases with identical schemas: it refuses on schema mismatch, orders tables parents-first by foreign keys, runs as a dry run unless --yes, replaces target rows via binary COPY in one transaction, resyncs identity sequences, verifies counts, and excludes schema_migrations and checkpoint tables.

test_migration_integrity.py is an integration test against the compose Postgres (skipped when unreachable) that guards preserved data (at least 96 documents, 29 graph_ingest_log rows, seed-order ids, advanced documents sequence, v2 content) rather than checking schema shape.

Schema consolidations were done by migration with data copied first: 0031 merged nine funder tables into five (funder_activity, documents, funders), 0033 folded credential_events into org_identifiers, and 0034 retired grants into funder_activity partner lines; org_identifiers is granted by column so new columns need an explicit column GRANT.

backend/app/db/pool.py exposes the shared pool three ways: get_pool/OwnerPoolDep give the raw owner pool (identity code, Import, seeds, tests may override); CallerPool/PoolDep wrap it so each REST connection is one transaction that SET LOCALs, in one statement, the Postgres role (anon or authenticated), the JWT claims from the request and a statement_timeout (DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS), returning to the pool as owner afterwards; and the agent_caller ContextVar carries the (role, claims) that Ask Sangam's SQL tools query as, defaulting to anon, applied through set_caller, which does not set a timeout so it never raises Ask's own lower one. A companion ContextVar, caveats_given, is a per-/agent-request set of tables whose caveats the SQL tools have already given in full, so repeats become one line; both are set by ask_access.

The proposals table (created in 0009) is a live server-side store: 0048_proposal_work adds NOT NULL jsonb columns work (everything the proposal screen and agent edit) and summary (list view, recomputed from work on every save); the repository runs as the caller, list_proposals never reads work, and save queues on a per-proposal asyncio lock, then locks the row with FOR UPDATE, applies a change function and writes work, summary, title and updated_at back in one transaction; proposals stays in the SQL catalog's KNOWN_EXCLUDED.

0048 changes write access: proposals_insert and proposals_update now allow org_id in app.my_match_org_ids() (org admins and stewards) or staff, so plain members read but no longer write proposals; documents_insert is widened to app.my_org_ids() or staff so any org role can upload to the Doc Vault, which org_id_for_member(write=False) mirrors in the upload routes; and the migration re-runs the guard that fails if a readable public table lacks a read policy.

documents.doc_type is free text with proposal-related values: proposal_template (a funder's application form, reserved so Import research cannot write it; funder_form picks the newest by fetched_at, replacing the dropped proposal_templates/template_items tables) and proposal_draft, which insert_draft writes as a private, AI-generated Doc Vault document (source_name 'Sangam Pitch', status received) for each saved proposal version.

The SQL catalog allowlists 37 tables and KNOWN_EXCLUDED names 23 deliberately withheld tables, including news_link_scores, news_watch, promotions, catalog_writes, deleted_documents and funder_match_details alongside the sensitive ones; the catalog also self-checks at import (columns, primary keys, foreign keys target catalogued tables).

db/scripts/truncate_all.sql (make db-clean) truncates every public table except schema_migrations with RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE, because dropping the ledger would make migrate replay everything, then restores the local dev user and marks it staff with auth_user_id.

Migration 0049_rfp_match_saved.sql only drops and re-adds rfp_matches_status_check so status may be flagged, saved, reviewed or dismissed (the baseline allowed only flagged, reviewed, dismissed), and needs no new policy or grant because the existing 0027 update policy already covers the column.

The rfps table group is rfps (funder calls with open/closed/removed status, deadline, amounts and provenance, unique on funder_id, title, deadline), rfp_tags, rfp_locations and rfp_matches; all four are allowlisted in the SQL catalog, and the catalog's rfp_matches status values include saved.

rfp_matches is org-private and update-only for callers: 0025 grants authenticated only UPDATE, 0027 gives a read policy to the org's people and staff and an update policy to app.my_writable_org_ids() (members and admins, not stewards) or staff; so rows must pre-exist, and flag_matches inserts one per org with members and per open, unexpired call sharing a domain (matched_by 'rules:domain', week_of) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING so re-runs never overwrite an org's choice.

The match status vocabulary is duplicated across layers: the DB CHECK constraint (0049), the RfpMatchUpdate schema Literal, and the SQL catalog's status values; update_match (PATCH /api/rfps/{id}/matches/{org_id}) sets status and stamps matched_by with the user's id, so adding a status requires changing all of them.

The RFP feed query (repositories/rfps.feed) runs as the caller and returns an org's saved calls regardless of the call's state, but non-dismissed calls only while the call is open and its deadline has not passed (date computed in Asia/Kolkata); can_act is derived from app.my_writable_org_ids() or staff.

public_sql.py holds SQL fragments shared by the public Registry list, profile facts, partner groups and news stories; private sources (staff datasets, Doc Vault) cite a synthetic URL on the reserved domain sangam.invalid (PRIVATE_SOURCE_DOMAIN in ingest/research/source_guards.py), and public_url/public_name return NULL and public_text drops text for such rows, as the SQL twin of source_guards.is_private_source.

registry_page_sql reads the Registry index, places, tags, programmes, partner counts, open calls, CSR years and story counts on the caller pool (RLS plus is_public/visibility decide visibility) but reads org_identifiers on-file types on the owner pool (_registered for the Registrations filter, _add_registrations for the page's orgs only, after the caller connection is returned) so filters are identical for every viewer; GET /api/registry fetches entity_research run counts (staff-only table) for the page's rows on the owner pool and drops them with a logged warning on failure rather than failing the list; IDENTIFIERS nulls the number and detail of non-public registrations and flags number_withheld.

make_pool builds the owner AsyncConnectionPool with min_size=1, autocommit, prepare_threshold=0, dict rows, an acquisition timeout (DB_POOL_TIMEOUT_S), a connect timeout, max_idle=300 and a check_connection health check on checkout; the server opens one in the lifespan sized by DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE, while standalone batch jobs (calls, news, matching runners) build their own small pools with explicit max_size and the same limits; concurrency gates (db_gate_slots) sit under the pool size so the checkpointer can still write.

LangGraph checkpoint tables are not created by SQL migrations or at boot: make migrate runs migrate_checkpointer (PostgresSaver.setup()) after the SQL files succeed, even when none were pending (--status only reports the version), and open_checkpointer does no DDL at boot but raises RuntimeError telling the operator to run make migrate when checkpoint_migrations is missing or not at CHECKPOINT_VERSION.

0051 and 0052 add DELETE grants and policies for callers: documents_delete lets staff delete only a private, org-owned vault_upload (DELETE /api/documents/{id}); proposals_delete lets org admins, stewards and staff delete proposals and documents_delete_draft lets them delete a private proposal_draft; repositories delete the row first and roll back if Storage cannot move the file to the trash, and delete_vault_upload refuses a document still referenced by chunks, extraction_log, document_links or a proposal draft.
0050_proposal_stage_shift is a data migration that moves proposals at step 3 or later up one step in both work and summary, because the Make a case step was inserted as step 3.

0053 adds deleted_documents and an AFTER DELETE trigger log_document_delete on documents (SECURITY DEFINER function app.log_document_delete, revoked from PUBLIC) that records the whole old row as jsonb, org_id and deleted_by for every delete path; the table has RLS with a staff-only SELECT policy, no grant to authenticated, nullable restored_by/restored_at columns, and is in the SQL catalog's KNOWN_EXCLUDED; a refused or rolled-back delete logs nothing.

Vault and proposal deletes are soft at the file level: storage.trash moves objects to trash/<key> inside the same bucket (restoring moved keys if a later move fails, and treating an already-missing key as success), and both DELETE /api/documents/{id} and DELETE /api/proposals/{id} use it instead of storage.remove, answering 502 and keeping the row when the move fails; storage.remove remains a hard delete used to discard an upload whose bytes do not match its extension.

The org-vault bucket's allowed_mime_types is set by 0054 and re-issued in full by 0055 (adding PowerPoint) to PDF, docx, xlsx, pptx, CSV, Markdown, plain text and PNG/JPEG/WebP, for both org-vault and org-vault-local; both migrations no-op without a storage schema, the same list lives in code as storage.VAULT_TYPES, and test_storage asserts the two match.

The Doc Vault upload routes validate types in code as well as in the bucket: the extension must be in storage.VAULT_TYPES (415) when a signed upload URL is requested and at confirm, and at confirm the bytes are read back and matched to a file signature (a mismatch removes the object and answers 415) before text is extracted and the documents row inserted; the stored content_hash is measured server-side from those bytes.

0056 tightens documents_insert with ALTER POLICY so a signed-in caller's row must have a null storage_path or one starting with org-vault/<org_id>/ in addition to the org-or-staff test, preventing a row from naming another org's vault file; owner-pool writes (library, staff datasets, seeds) are unaffected, and storage.owned_split and the confirm route enforce the same ownership rule in code.

fetch_page (repositories/paging.py) is the shared paging helper for ten list repositories (contacts, documents, funders, meta tags/locations, orgs, partner lines, programs, rfps, scores): it requires SQL selecting COUNT(*) OVER () AS total whose outermost ORDER BY ends in id with no LIMIT, semicolon or comment after it (else ValueError before any query), appends LIMIT/OFFSET, reads the total from the first row, and for an empty page past the end runs one extra count query so the total still reports the whole list.

Paged list responses share Page[T] (items, total, limit, offset), validated by PageParams (limit 1-100, default 50, offset >= 0), and FacetedPage[T] adds counts (bucket cards) and facets (dropdown options as Facet value/count); facets.ordered sorts options most common first, ties A-Z ignoring case, with SDGs in number order; RegistryPage is FacetedPage[RegistryRow].

GET /api/registry is paged, filtered, searched and counted in Postgres by registry_page_sql: one statement builds a lean per-entity index CTE (the same fragments the displayed rows use), applies filters and substring search, orders CSOs first then funders by lower(name) then id with LIMIT/OFFSET and returns the total of every kept row; only the page's orgs and funders then get pipelined detail queries, and the route drops the search field from the response.

Registry bucket counts and dropdown options cover the whole Registry regardless of filters but are computed only for offset 0 (later pages return empty counts and facets, with the facet counting cut from the Postgres plan); filter scope is kind-specific: reg applies only to type=cso, ftype and approach only to type=funder.
